title: A lower payment: a cheaper loan?
hook: Stretch a loan and the monthly payment drops. What happens to the total?

doesNotKnow: that a lower monthly payment over a longer term can cost much more in total
that interest is charged for every month money stays owed

misconception: A lower payment means a cheaper loan.
objective: The learner can explain that a longer term lowers each payment but keeps the balance owed for longer, so the total interest rises: on $20,000 at 6%, going from 5 to 7 years costs about $1,343 more.

claims.text: A level monthly payment on a loan P at monthly rate r over n months is P·r / (1 − (1 + r)^−n).
claims.source: Present value of an annuity solved for the payment. Standard, e.g. Brealey, Myers & Allen, Principles of Corporate Finance, ch. 2 (annuities).

claims.text: $20,000 at 6% a year (0.5% a month) over 5 years: $386.66 a month, $3,199 total interest.
Over 7 years: $292.17 a month, $4,542 total interest.
Stretching from 5 to 7 years cuts the payment by about $95 a month and adds about $1,343 of interest.
The stage's payments and interest for other terms (2 to 8 years) use the same formula, e.g. 2 years: $886.41 a month, $1,274 interest; 8 years: $262.83 a month, $5,232 interest.
A longer loan repays the balance more slowly, so more money stays owed each month and is charged interest.
claims.source: Monthly interest = 0.5% × balance still owed; with a smaller payment the balance falls more slowly, so the sum of monthly interest over more months is larger.

claims.text: The lesson is a model: a fixed, illustrative 6% rate, level monthly payments, no fees. It is not a current market rate.
claims.source: Assumptions of the lesson's own calculation in Demo.tsx.

recall.question: Same car loan, same rate. Option A: 4 years. Option B: 6 years, with a lower monthly payment. Which costs more in total?
options: B, you pay interest for more months
recall.why: Interest is charged on what is still owed each month. A longer loan keeps more owed for longer, so total interest rises even as the payment falls.
